body: Are there updates on when this fix will be merged?
Hi @rubennorte could you take a look ?
Update on this one? https://snyk.io/test/npm/axios/0.18.0

@emilyemorehouse would you be able to review this when you get a chance? The DoS vulnerability was recently published on Snyk (https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-174505) and may be causing some CI pipelines to fail
Both Snyk and SourceClear (SC had it for quite some time): https://www.sourceclear.com/vulnerability-database/vulnerabilities/6130

Hello,

Please correct me if I am wrong, but it looks like all that is needed here is a one line change that was submitted via a PR more than a year ago. It also looks like all tests have passed on that PR. 

I am very appreciative of the work that has gone into this project. I have quite a few projects of my own that depend on the awesome work contributed here. If there is additional work that needed to be done for this I would be happy and proud to pitch in.

Is there a way we can get this PR merged and released to close the security vulnerability? I would really like to continue to use this project, but I have a responsibility to ensure that the projects that I maintain are free from vulnerabilities. 

Thank you for the continued efforts on this project and please let me know if there is something I can contribute to help close the vulnerability and add value to this project.
Glad to see this is merged. Does anybody know when would be the next stable release?
The latest build failed: https://travis-ci.org/axios/axios/jobs/529505165

There's a nested dependency with native code that doesn't seem to support Node 12. I'll make a PR to lower the Node version that the CI uses so that the rest of the build can run

Edit: Opened PR #2138
As soon as CI is green, I'll issue a release!

We've tried this code and there appears to be some situations where `stream` is not yet defined resulting in errors like this:

```
{
    "errorMessage": "stream is not defined",
    "errorType": "ReferenceError",
    "stackTrace": [
        "dispatchHttpRequest (/var/task/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:219:13)",
        "new Promise (<anonymous>)",
        "httpAdapter (/var/task/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:18:10)",
        "dispatchRequest (/var/task/node_modules/axios/lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:59:10)",
        "<anonymous>",
        "process._tickDomainCallback (internal/process/next_tick.js:228:7)"
    ]
}
```

@emilyemorehouse i would not recommend releasing until this is addressed.

I am sorry to say that I have experienced this issue as well:

`(node:4825) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: ReferenceError: stream is not defined
    at dispatchHttpRequest (/home/travis/build/Luidog/fms-api-client/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:219:13)
    at new Promise (<anonymous>)
    at httpAdapter (/home/travis/build/Luidog/fms-api-client/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:18:10)
    at dispatchRequest (/home/travis/build/Luidog/fms-api-client/node_modules/axios/lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:59:10)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:89:5)`
Can we just wrap it in a null check before destroying?

Thanks @rajivshah3, working on remediating it.

@hughns @Luidog have you experienced the no stream defined from applying the snyk patch or from the recent change merged to this repo?

One more ping @rajivshah3 @hughns @Luidog - not sure which one of you uses the Snyk patch but heads up that we've updated it a couple of hours ago and if you re-run `snyk protect` it should download the new version (or in any other issue you could re-apply the patch).

@rajivshah3 Well spotted! I should have added that this was via snyk (and that I have raised a ticket with snyk support too). We haven't tested with the 0.19.0-beta.1 release yet.

@lirantal Yes, we saw the issue after the snyk patch was applied. The support ticket is https://support.snyk.io/hc/en-us/requests/445
Thanks for the quick response @lirantal ! The patch looks good now
Great to hear, thanks for the update both!
@lirantal, I did indeed used the original snyk patch which caused the test failures. I have rerun the `snyk protect` and now the patch is applied correctly. Thank you for following up on this.

@Luidog great news, thanks!

any chance you or @hughns have a way to reproduce the problem for the undefined stream variable that you experienced?
Apologies if it's veering offtopic for this thread, but is there a mechanism to tell the Snyk folks when an issue has been remediated in a new release?

@schmod you can always give us a ping through support@snyk.io or security@snyk.io. I'm happy to also take this offline with you through twitter (I'm at https://www.twitter.com/liran_tal) and be a source of contact or any other security related help I can provide

Where does this fix stand in terms of a stable release? Is it feasible to have it released soon? (With the correct fix of course).

I can help work on it if needed, but we would need to get rid of axios otherwise on an open source SDK I'm actively maintaining (which I would prefer to avoid, it's a great library!)

I think @emilyemorehouse said a new release can be created once CI is green. The problem is that it's failing due to an unrelated issue where a dependency won't build on the current version of NodeJS. I fixed it in #2138 but it hasn't been merged yet
@lirantal I will send you a reproduction via email - security@snyk.io
thanks @Luidog, appreciate it!
When would be the next release?
Any update on when this change will be released?

Just received a notice from Github itself telling me that this is a serious vulnerability. 

"Known high severity security vulnerability detected in axios <= 0.18.0 defined in package.json."

@emilyemorehouse are you guys able to do a patch release for the vulnerability issue? I am aware that there are other commits for features in between.

Cherry-picking the commits into, for example, `next` branch for the patch release should work.

Hi @emilyemorehouse, as others have said is there any update on when a patch version can be released? This has been merged for a fair few weeks now and we really need to get a fix out, especially seeing as we're now getting Github notifications on this.
+1 subscribing for the patch release so that we can update our versions.

Might be better to click the `Subscribe` button for this PR instead of commenting with a `+1` 🙂 That way you'll be notified without creating notifications or emails for everyone else.

![Subscribe button screenshot](https://image.prntscr.com/image/-gY3jeYiR6OBY8NO9SL3Dw.png)
@pxgamer yes. Thank you for this comment. However, there are still people doing the `+1` thing

@emilyemorehouse There hasn't been a new release since 0.18.0 in August of 2018. Can we at least get some sort of patch? There are multiple critical fixes that have been merged and _need_ releasing.

Thanks

> @emilyemorehouse There hasn't been a new release since 0.18.0 in August of 2018. Can we at least get some sort of patch? There are multiple critical fixes that have been merged and _need_ releasing.
> 
> Thanks

Yes, they are working on a new release once the CI turns green. 

Remember this is Open Source, the contributors and maintainers have to carve out personal time to help out the community, this does delay a few things. 

If it is critical for you you can use the current master for your use.

I've actually been using a forked version since months ago. My complaint is that the release process is too slow. Not a single patch in almost a year's time?

The more you ball up changes, the slower and higher impact (positive or, god forbid, negative) your next release will be. Many software shops have already demonstrated that you build more reliable software by releasing in small chunks, frequently.

That's all I'm trying to encourage here.
@heisian I agree with you on the release cycle, we’ve been using the patch too.

Precisely, and I'm sure many production shops are _not_ using the original version of Axios for the same reason.

When a security vulnerability like today's goes out, all these pent-up merges prevent us from responding quickly.

Now we have to wait for _other_ merges to pass before even being able to address the critical one.

Not to mention the possibility that some of these new features not related to the security advisory have the possibility of introducing bugs.

All of these things are pretty routine, but things here could most _definitely_ be alleviated by just making small patched releases instead of waiting this long.

@hemanthg4 [CI _is_ green on master](https://travis-ci.org/axios/axios/branches). This fix has been merged to master.

I maintain and have maintained OSS projects, and appreciate the work that maintainers put in. That said, requesting an `npm publish` of a branch that's green on CI should not be controversial. Especially not when it is related to a critical vuln, and when said release can be made opt-in e.g. via `beta` or `patch` markers.
@hemanthg4 CI is already green that is why I asked if they can release a patch version anytime soon.

This is even worse! We're green and have no way to post a new release. If I were maintaining the package, I would just make a patch `0.18.1` that includes the CVE fix _only_, then work on releasing other bits of the codebase.
Expect more attention (like me) on this issue as Github is now alerting on this vulnerability. CVE-2019-10742
The fix for this has been released in version 0.19.0

Thank you @emilyemorehouse!!

![thankyouDog](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/721128/58653190-2ca97180-82e3-11e9-8f92-66be1388c4f0.gif)

Thanks @emilyemorehouse for releasing this critical update. It is a great & invaluable service to the community.

Going forward, how do we see more frequent releases? Many other bugfixes/features were just sitting for almost an entire year. Is it a matter of bandwidth - do we need additional active maintainers?
i.e., it shouldn't take a serious vulnerability to be exposed to force us to release the rest of the pending changes. I would be glad to help if it is an issue of bandwidth.
Thanks @emilyemorehouse !! 🚀
